messages:
Arjun: FYI seeing 95th/99th latency spikes on the shared-gpu pool starting ~09:12 UTC. p99 jumped from ~80ms to ~650ms for small generate calls. Pls take a look, suspect noisy neighbor + kernel fallback.

Maria: copying some quick numbers from infra dashboards — overall GPU utilization for pool-shared-1 jumped to 98% at 09:10, memory pinned at ~91%. No obvious infra restarts.

Keegan: I rolled out adaptive_kernel_selector v2 ~07:30 today (staged). It switches kernel choices based on sequence length distribution and tries int8 kernels when safe. If it misclassifies, it can fall back to generic kernels which are slower.

Linh: can you paste the runtime profiler snippet? want to see if there's constant-time kernel fallback or KV cache thrash.

Arjun: profiler excerpt below (trimmed):
```
timestamp 09:12:28
model: redwood-llm-3b
avg_seq_len: 96
batch_size: 8 -> observed batching collapsed to 1-2 for many requests
kernel_selection: layer_3 fallback->generic_fp32, layer_7: int8_ok
cuda_time_kernel_generic_fp32: 420ms
cuda_time_kernel_int8: 28ms
kv_cache_evictions: 23/min (sustained)
queue_length: spikes to 120
```

Keegan: that kernel_generic_fp32 time is huge — suggests the fallback is happening for a hot path. Why is batching collapsing? batching heuristics usually aggregate across tenants; maybe tenant behavior caused many single-sample, long-context requests.

Maria: checked request patterns: tenant-78 and tenant-1234 had a surge of small interactive requests. tenant-1234 also has a couple of very long context traces (context ~8k tokens) which forces different kernel code-paths and large KV cache pressure.

PerfBot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0456 - noisy-tenant-causing-shared-pool-degradation (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0456)

Linh: KV cache evictions at 23/min is suspicious. Our prefix-cache TTL is 10m; long contexts can push out hot prefixes and increase cache misses which kills batching (requests wait on KV loads). Also if the kernel selector sees high seq_len it might choose kernels incompatible with cached KV layout -> fallback.

Arjun: I grabbed nvidia-smi and process list snapshot from the node:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86       CUDA Version: 12.1     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   PID   Type   Proc name               Usage(MiB)    %GPU            |
|    0  4211  C+G    redwood-runtime           12345MiB     98%              |
|    0  8192  C      tenant-sandbox           2048MiB      5%               |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Keegan: interesting — there's a sandboxed tenant worker here but the runtime process dominates mem. Are we running per-tenant cgroups? SRE had a patch to enforce per-tenant GPU mem limits but it might not have been applied to the shared pool nodes.

Maria: confirmed: the cgroup enforcement PR (ops#2123) was applied only to dedicated pools, not shared pools. Ops oversight.

Linh: mitigation suggestions: 1) apply per-tenant GPU mem limits to shared pool nodes (fast but intrusive), 2) temporarily throttle tenant-1234 rate or move it to a dedicated tenant pool, 3) roll back adaptive_kernel_selector v2 to v1 (prevents misclassification), 4) increase KV cache capacity for short term.

Arjun: I put a temporary throttle on tenant-1234 to 30 rps and bumped its slot to dedicated-burst. Immediate p99 dropped to ~120ms within 2 minutes.

Keegan: rolling back adaptive_kernel_selector to v1 in canary now. I'll watch kernel logs for fallback events.

PerfBot: Rollback action executed by Keegan at 09:30 UTC.

Maria: ops is patching the shared pool node config to enable per-tenant cgroup gpu memory enforcement. ETA 40m.

Linh: for post-incident follow-ups we should: - add a kernel-selection telemetry metric that tracks "fallback_count" per-layer per-tenant - surface KV cache eviction rate in the console per-tenant - add a soft per-tenant batching isolation (limit how many single-sample long-context requests can starve batch formation)

Arjun: agreed. Also add an alert: p99 > 300ms for 5m on shared pools -> auto throttle top offending tenant automatically (tooling to pick tenant with highest token/sec).

Keegan: note for investigation: why did the selector classify many medium-length requests as large? logging shows we were using a short window (5m) to compute seq_len distribution; need to expand to 30m to smooth out spikes.

Maria: filing follow-up tasks on the incident ticket for ops, runtime, and devex to add dashboard tiles. Linking INC-2026-0456.

Arjun: thanks all. current state: throttled tenant-1234, rollback in progress, cgroup patch deployed to shared nodes in 40m. I'll update when green. :white_check_mark:

Keegan: quick note — no customer-facing errors reported, just elevated latency. Good catch. :thumbsup:

Linh: postmortem owners: Arjun (runtime lead), Maria (infra), Keegan (selector). PerfBot assigned.

PerfBot: Incident INC-2026-0456 updated: postmortem scheduled, severity: sev3.
